title: chi_field.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: The chi-field evolves as a scalar field in 1+1D according to the Klein-Gordon equation with phi^4 self-interaction and a grace source term.
definitions: chi(x,t): scalar field value at spatial point x and time t
J_grace: grace source term = _G * Phi * tanh(chi) / (S_local + )
: small positive number preventing division by zero
derivation: The equation of motion is chi + mchi + chi = J_grace(x,t).
Spatial dimension is discretized using second-order finite differences, converting the PDE into a system of ODEs in time.
Time integration uses RK4 with Neumann boundary conditions.
Parameter scans over m and  classify stability regimes.
canonical_node.action: Implement and run the ChiFieldSolver class to numerically solve the chi-field PDE in 1+1D, including parameter scans and stability analysis.
boundary: Does not provide analytical proofs of existence or uniqueness.
Does not extend to higher spatial dimensions.
Does not include coupling to other fields beyond the grace source.
Does not claim physical reality; it is a numerical implementation.
test: Energy drift < 0.5% over 1000 time steps with 128 spatial points and dt=0.01.
Stability phase diagram reproduces expected bands for canonical parameters.
Dispersion relation  = k + m holds for linear modes.

dg1_dependencies: MasterEquation class (Lagrangian mechanics of 10-variable point system)

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a numerical PDE solver for the chi-field, enabling spatial and temporal evolution studies beyond point mechanics.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the core chi-field dynamics as a field theory, consistent with the point system limit when spatial gradients vanish.

kill_conditions: If the notebook is not reproducible due to missing dependencies or code errors.

plain_summary: This document describes a Google Colab notebook that implements a numerical solver for the chi-field as a 1+1D Klein-Gordon equation with phi^4 self-interaction and a grace source term. It uses method of lines with finite differences and RK4 integration. The notebook includes parameter scans and reports stability and energy conservation. It is a numerical implementation, not a proof of physical reality.
